poc: Bench-only first: standard Gast exhaust is lubricated. Collect/vent it away from people; do not use it as the person-facing cooling outlet.
Use the existing rated cylinder pressure-reduction package. Set motor running pressure to its chosen curve point, not cylinder pressure.

Use a guarded, rated brake or generator/load with torque and rpm measurement. For the lower-duty 2AM target: about 200 W and 1.91 Nm at 1000 rpm. This is a target, not a purchased complete load station.
Record tank pressure/temperature, motor inlet pressure/temperature, exhaust pressure, low-speed bulk exhaust temperature, actual mass flow and shaft torque/rpm simultaneously.
Use a short insulated, low-mass collection section; its UA=1 W/K calculation is a design sensitivity, not measured conductance. Keep exhaust pressure loss low and measure it.

Run a regulator-only bypass at comparable measured flow; it separates Joule-Thomson/line cooling from incremental motor cooling. Record any flow change rather than treating unlike cases as a controlled comparison.

Precondition until the measured source state is repeatable, with exhaust away from the target. Then record repeated up-to-10 s demonstration pulses. Do not promise first-pulse cooling: warm motor/nozzle metal can absorb much of the nominal cooling budget.

Show cooling with calibrated simultaneous temperatures, not a cold housing, IR image or skin sensation. Use a predeclared demonstration screen such as a repeatable >=5 K bulk drop across the motor with sensor uncertainty much smaller than that drop; this is a test criterion, not a predicted result.

Check steady first-law closure: Q_into_motor = Wshaft - mdot cp (Tin-Tout), with kinetic-temperature correction if required. During startup include motor/fixture thermal storage; do not interpret it as steady heat leak.
A regulator-only measured cold-air result is a legitimate throttling POC. It does not validate a motor expander or prove outdoor 20-50 cm cooling.

limits: No new CFD, CAD fit, Lean proof or hardware temperature guarantee
Power and flow must refer to the same operating point; supplier headline maximum values are not arbitrarily paired
Gast point estimates read from curves and interpolate pressure; motor inlet-temperature dependence, leakage, casing heat and exhaust backpressure are unresolved
Negative calculated exhaust temperatures do not establish approved continuous subzero operation
Short-path UA=1 W/K is an assumption; motor metal and nozzle wall startup are not represented in the steady calculation
Gas inventory runtimes exclude startup conditioning, leaks, regulator dropout and cold operating limits
Prices are public US listings in USD before taxes/freight; no offer, payment, inquiry or order sent
